title: Article 10 — Continuance of the rights of citizenship

content.overview: Article 10 provides that every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India under any of the foregoing provisions of Part II shall, subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament, continue to be such citizen.
content.glance: Citizenship under Arts 5–9 continues, subject to parliamentary law (Art 11 / Citizenship Act).
content.study:
Article 10 is a continuance clause.

Effect: Persons who are citizens (or deemed citizens) under Articles 5–9 continue as citizens, but subject to any law made by Parliament.

Link to Article 11: Parliament’s power to regulate citizenship includes power to provide for termination, deprivation and other incidents. Article 10 therefore preserves commencement citizenship while expressly subordinating its continuance to parliamentary legislation.

Examination: state that continuance is not absolute; it yields to parliamentary law under Article 11 (Citizenship Act, 1955 and amendments).

sections.heading: Textual effect
sections.body: Citizenship (or deemed citizenship) under Articles 5–9 continues, subject to parliamentary law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 10.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 10 provides that every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India under any of the foregoing provisions of Part II shall continue to be such citizen, subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament. Continuance is therefore subject to the Citizenship Act, 1955 and other parliamentary laws under Article 11.

examTips: Continuance is subject to parliamentary law — not absolute.
content.migrationNote: QUAL remediation 2026-10-09: continuance subject to Art 11 clarified.

keyTakeaways: Art 10: continuance of Arts 5–9 citizenship subject to parliamentary law.
